statement: Theorem A (prime-field index calculus, restricted XL/Macaulay model): at arity m = 2 on a prime-order E(F_p) with n = #E, any factor base presented as a radical ideal (auxiliary variables allowed), with relations taken from the unsplit Semaev polynomial S_3 plus the base equations solved by XL, cost charged as the full XL rank with a fresh rank per target, a relation counted only when exposed through a block-1 univariate, at least c*|B| relations required (axiom A3) and uniform independent targets, has expected cost E[cost] >= c*sqrt(n); so in that model index calculus at m = 2 cannot beat Pollard rho's exponent 1/2. The bound needs two axioms the adversarial checker found implicit in the proof: (1) each attempt yields at most one relation, or cost is at least the number of relations output; (2) A3 holds, which excludes bases with known logarithms such as B = {iP}.
